quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not brake, as this may also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials all the time helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What should you do with your eyes when turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: Look down at the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your whole body to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Check that the clutch works smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve.
questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work properly. Clean and adjust the mirrors. Make sure the fuel supply valve is OPEN, not closed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride below the speed limit.
Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: What happens if you shift to a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle may lurch and the front tire may skid.
The motorcycle may lurch and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle may lurch and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down enough before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is slowing down by turning off the engine.
It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
It damages the engine and is not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it slows your motorcycle similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Prevent brakes from working on dry roads.
Warn you when brake pads need replacing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent skidding and wheel lock-up.
questions.explanation: ABS is designed to prevent skidding and wheel lock-up when you brake hard in a straight line. When sensors detect a wheel about to lock, the system releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep maximum braking power.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may interfere with the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load too high raises your motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is located next to the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: When a rider extends their left arm straight out, it means they plan to turn left or change lanes to the left. Hand signals can be used instead of or along with turn signals.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Practice riding on an empty road.
Flash your lights so others can see you.
Practice riding on the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on an empty road.
questions.explanation: Practice on a quiet road first to get used to how your motorcycle handles with a passenger. The extra weight changes how it rides.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips under five miles long, just a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright-colored clothing whenever you ride. Crashes happen at any time of day or night, so stay visible at all times.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provides protection in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, ideally leather, to protect yourself. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in warm weather while protecting you from injury.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle rider check their mirrors?

options.text: More often than the amount time spent looking ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to see what is behind you and spot potential dangers.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, it is best to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may just make them tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: Studies show that when motorcycles have their headlights turned on during the day:

options.text: They are not as easy to see as other vehicles.
They are more visible to other drivers than when their headlights are turned off.
They are less safe than when their headlights are turned off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more visible to other drivers than when their headlights are turned off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride to help other drivers see you. During the day, a motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as noticeable.

questions.question: After drinking, what lessens the effects of alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver breaks down alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is correct?

options.text: You can complete a pass in a no passing zone.
You can go 10 mph over the speed limit to complete a pass.
You must start and finish a pass only in a passing zone.
You must complete a pass on the shoulder if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish a pass only in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Passing must happen within posted speed limits and only where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay away from parked cars to avoid hazards like opening doors or people stepping out. This positioning keeps you safe from unexpected dangers.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a tire go flat. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is the usual sign of tire failure.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes. One controls the front wheel and one controls the rear wheel.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, what should you do?

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Do not worry about your lane position.
Always ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors.
